blockdesc-buckingmill-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically powered gang saw that cross-cuts tree trunks into logs. Fit two saw sashes, a crankshaft and two blade kits to assemble it.
error-need-sash: Each blade kit goes into a saw sash. Fit another sash first.
error-blades-fitted: Both blade kits are already fitted.
error-blade-metal: Both blade kits must be the same metal. This mill has {0} blades.
error-not-a-part: That is not a part of this mill.
error-trunk-cut: The trunk is cut too far to take out.
error-no-logging: This mill cannot work with the installed Logging Expanded.
error-incomplete: Assemble the mill before loading a trunk.
error-bed-full: There is already a trunk in the mill.
info-committed: Too far cut to take the trunk out
info-nopower: Not turning fast enough, connect a turning axle
handbook-assembly-text: Place the frame where the whole machine has room, then fit Immersive Woodworking's sawmill parts with rightmouse, in any order: two saw sashes, a crankshaft and two blade kits of the same metal. Each blade kit goes into a sash, so fit a sash before each kit. No carriage or feed levers are needed. ctrl + rightmouse takes a blade kit back out. The other parts come back only when you break the frame, which drops every fitted part.
handbook-power-text: Connect a turning axle to the power side of the frame. The assembled mill is a heavy load, twice a plank sawmill's, and it only cuts while its shaft turns at a fair speed. Until it is assembled it barely loads the shaft.
handbook-trunks-text: The mill cuts Logging Expanded tree trunks of any size, one at a time. Trunks must have their branches removed first while Logging Expanded asks for that. Load a trunk with rightmouse, holding it, or with an empty hand to take one from your hotbar or backpack. A trunk storage rack standing against the infeed side, on the ground, feeds the running mill: it takes the rack's top trunk about once a second whenever it is empty. A branched trunk on top of the rack holds the line until you deal with it. ctrl + rightmouse takes the trunk back out, but only before a quarter of it is cut.
handbook-yield-text:
Every log stored in a trunk takes 8 turns of the shaft and gives 2 logs of its wood, which drop out of the output side. A cut trunk's resin and branches are lost, as on a sawhorse.

Each blade kit loses 1 durability for every 4 logs stored in a cut trunk, rounded up. A worn out kit breaks and the mill stops until a new one is fitted. These figures are the defaults of ModConfig/buckingsawmill.json.
